chapter: Funerals, second lines and being an outsider
title: Jazz funerals today, orderly second lines and umbrellas
summary: They discuss funerals for musicians, Wood never saw second lines unruly or fights, and contrasts tattered umbrellas then with fancy ones now.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well, I have marched with a family at a funeral, you know, which is a little different, but, you know, I was asked to do that.
Yeah.
And it seems like so many musicians have died since you were here in the 50s.
Well, I gather now that that's about the only time you really have a jazz funeral is when a musician dies.
No, they have other times.
Do they? Yeah.
There's a lot of stuff going on that you don't hear about.
Yeah.
But it's, the second line has really gotten unruly.
Yeah.
Did you ever see them get really unruly?
No.
Misbehaved? Never? No. That's interesting.

They were always on the sidewalk, close to the band, you know, up next to it. They would surge back and forth, but I've never seen them get unruly and I've never seen them really interfere in any way with the procession itself, the progress of the thing.
They didn't bump into the trombone player and knock his teeth out.
No. No. No. No. No, indeed. Nothing like that.
I don't remember a lot of fights or anything like that.

I don't remember ever seeing a fight. That's one of the striking things to me, going to those parades, that they would fill the streets and they would have these huge second lines, but there never seemed to be any real, any angry people or any really sort of conflict. It was something that people just sort of shared in and enjoyed. And I'm amused now, too, to see these second lines that get tricked up for the bands that play down the French Quarter and other places, where they have these umbrellas that have precise frills all around them in different colors. That is just so totally away from what those second lines were 30 years ago. They had umbrellas, but the ideal one would be nothing but ribs and a few tatters of black umbrella fabric hanging down. And to have one of those really frilly, fancy ones, it just seems very alien to me.
It's very phony to me. Sometimes people would come out and look like they deliberately dressed down, shall we say, and would get a beat-up umbrella.
Oh, yeah. The more beat-up it was, I think the more desirable it was.
No fabric at all.
Yeah, just the bare ribs. Yeah. I don't want to forget this.
